subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Copper is ___ useful metal. (UP B.Ed 2019)
explanation: Although 'useful' starts with a vowel letter 'u', it starts with a consonant sound /juː/. Therefore, 'a' is the correct article.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: ___ Ganga is a sacred river. (UP B.Ed 2020)
explanation: We use the definite article 'The' before the names of rivers, seas, oceans, and mountain ranges. Hence, 'The Ganga' is correct.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: He is ___ honorable man. (UP B.Ed 2021)
explanation: The word 'honorable' starts with a silent 'h', so the initial sound is a vowel /ɒ/. Therefore, we use the indefinite article 'an'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct articles to fill in the blanks: French is ___ language of ___ people of France.
explanation: 'French is the language (particular language) of the people of France (particular population).' Both nouns are specific, requiring 'the'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: The guide knows ___ way. (UP B.Ed 2018)
explanation: 'Way' refers to the specific route that the guide knows to lead the tourists. Thus, the definite article 'the' is correct.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Sri Lanka is ___ island in the Indian Ocean.
explanation: The noun 'island' starts with the vowel sound /aɪ/, so the indefinite article 'an' is appropriate here.

subject: English Grammar
text: Identify the correct article to fill in the blank: She returned after ___ hour.
explanation: In 'hour', the letter 'h' is silent, and it starts with the vowel sound /aʊ/. Hence, 'an' is correct.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Honest men speak ___ truth. (UP B.Ed 2023)
explanation: The idiom/phrase is 'speak the truth' where 'truth' is treated as a specific and unique concept.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct article: I first saw him ___ year ago.
explanation: The word 'year' starts with the consonant sound /j/ (as in 'yacht'). Therefore, the correct indefinite article is 'a'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: ___ Sun shines brightly.
explanation: The definite article 'The' is used before nouns that are unique or one of their kind, such as the Sun, Moon, Earth.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: I bought ___ horse, ___ ox, and ___ buffalo. (UP B.Ed 2017)
explanation: 'Horse' starts with consonant /h/, 'ox' starts with vowel sound /ɒ/, and 'buffalo' starts with consonant /b/. Hence, 'a, an, a' is correct.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Wisdom is ___ gift of heaven.
explanation: When an abstract noun is qualified by a descriptive phrase (like 'of heaven'), it takes the definite article 'the'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: He hopes to join ___ university soon.
explanation: 'University' begins with the consonant sound /juː/, requiring the indefinite article 'a'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: The teacher was angry ___ his behavior. (UP B.Ed 2021)
explanation: We are angry 'with' a person, but angry 'at' someone's behavior, conduct, or a situation.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: He has been suffering ___ fever since yesterday. (UP B.Ed 2020)
explanation: The verb 'suffer' is followed by the preposition 'from' when denoting an illness or disease.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct preposition: She is proficient ___ English. (UP B.Ed 2019)
explanation: The adjective 'proficient' takes the preposition 'in' when expressing competence in a subject, language, or skill.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: The old man died ___ cholera. (UP B.Ed 2022)
explanation: 'Die of' is used when a person dies directly of a disease, hunger, thirst, or old age.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Please abstain ___ evil habits. (UP B.Ed 2023)
explanation: The verb 'abstain' is always followed by the preposition 'from' (abstain from voting, smoking, evil habits, etc.).

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: He is fond ___ music.
explanation: The adjective 'fond' takes the fixed preposition 'of' to mean having a liking for something.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: The dog ran ___ the road. (UP B.Ed 2018)
explanation: 'Across' means from one side to the other, which fits the movement of running from one side of the road to another.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct preposition: We must adapt ourselves ___ changing circumstances.
explanation: The reflexive verb 'adapt (oneself)' takes the preposition 'to' when adjusting to new environments or situations.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: He was accused ___ theft.
explanation: The verb 'accuse' is followed by 'of' to denote the crime or charge (accused of murder/theft).

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: I am senior ___ him by two years.
explanation: Latin comparative adjectives ending in '-ior' (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) are followed by 'to' instead of 'than'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Do not interfere ___ my private affairs. (UP B.Ed 2017)
explanation: We say 'interfere in' (a matter/affair) when involving ourselves in something without invitation, and 'interfere with' when obstructing something.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct preposition: The plane flew ___ the clouds.
explanation: 'Above' is used when something is at a higher level than another thing, which fits flying higher than a layer of clouds.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: She has been waiting for you ___ three hours.
explanation: 'For' is used to show a duration of time (three hours), whereas 'since' denotes a specific starting point in the past.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Divide the apples ___ the two brothers.
explanation: 'Between' is used for sharing or distributing between two people or things, while 'among' is used for more than two.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: The hunter aimed ___ the bird. (UP B.Ed 2024)
explanation: The verb 'aim' takes the preposition 'at' to point towards a target.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct verb form: She ___ in Delhi for ten years before moving to Mumbai.
explanation: The Past Perfect tense ('had lived') is used to describe an action that was completed before another action in the past (moving to Mumbai).

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank with the correct tense: If you ___ hard, you will pass the exam. (UP B.Ed 2022)
explanation: In the first conditional (possible future condition), the conditional clause uses Simple Present ('work'), and the main clause uses Simple Future.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct form of verb: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius. (UP B.Ed 2018)
explanation: Scientific facts, general truths, and habits are always expressed in the Simple Present tense ('boils' for singular 'Water').

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: When I reached the station, the train ___.
explanation: When two past actions are related, the one that happened first is in the Past Perfect ('had left') and the second is in Simple Past ('reached').

subject: English Grammar
text: Identify the tense of the given sentence: 'They have been playing since morning.' (UP B.Ed 2020)
explanation: The structure 'have/has + been + verb-ing' represents the Present Perfect Continuous tense, describing an action that started in the past and is still ongoing.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: I ___ him since we graduated.
explanation: The word 'since' indicates a period of time from the past up to the present. The Present Perfect tense ('haven't seen') is required here.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: We ___ a movie when the power went out.
explanation: An ongoing action in the past is interrupted by another action (Simple Past). The ongoing action should be in Past Continuous ('were watching').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct verb form: By this time next year, I ___ my degree. (UP B.Ed 2021)
explanation: The phrase 'By this time next year' implies a deadline in the future, which requires the Future Perfect tense ('will have completed').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct option: She usually ___ tea, but today she is drinking coffee.
explanation: 'Usually' signals a habitual action, which requires the Simple Present tense ('drinks' for third-person singular 'She').

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: My mother ___ the dinner before my father arrived.
explanation: The action of cooking occurred before the father's arrival in the past. Therefore, the first action must be in Past Perfect ('had cooked').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct sentence: (UP B.Ed 2019)
explanation: Verbs of possession like 'have' are stative and cannot be used in continuous tenses. 'He has many friends' is correct.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: I wish I ___ a king. (UP B.Ed 2023)
explanation: In hypothetical wishes and imaginary/subjunctive structures, 'were' is used for all subject pronouns (I, he, she, they).

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct verb form: They ___ to the zoo last Sunday.
explanation: 'Last Sunday' is a past time indicator. The Simple Past tense ('went') is used for actions completed at a specific past time.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct verb form: It ___ since last night. (UP B.Ed 2017)
explanation: Since the action started in the past (last night) and is still continuing, and a duration/point of time is mentioned ('since'), we use Present Perfect Continuous.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct option: I ___ my homework yet.
explanation: The adverb 'yet' is commonly used with negative sentences in the Present Perfect tense ('have not finished').

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: If I had known you were coming, I ___ you at the airport. (UP B.Ed 2022)
explanation: This is a Third Conditional sentence representing an imaginary past condition. Structure: If + Past Perfect, would have + Past Participle.

subject: English Grammar
text: Complete the sentence: If it rains, the match ___ called off. (UP B.Ed 2020)
explanation: This is a First Conditional sentence representing a real future possibility. Structure: If + Simple Present, Simple Future ('will be').

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: If I ___ you, I would accept the offer.
explanation: This is a Second Conditional sentence representing an imaginary present/future condition. Subjunctive 'were' is used in the 'if' clause.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: If she had studied harder, she ___ the test.
explanation: Third Conditional sentence structure requires 'would have + past participle' in the main clause because the 'if' clause is in the past perfect tense.

subject: English Grammar
text: Complete the conditional sentence: If you heat ice, it ___.
explanation: This is a Zero Conditional sentence representing a general truth or physical law. Both clauses use Simple Present tense.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Unless you ___ harder, you will not succeed.
explanation: The conditional clause with 'unless' takes Simple Present ('work') to refer to a future condition. Simple Future is not used inside conditional clauses.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: If he ___ earlier, he would have caught the bus. (UP B.Ed 2019)
explanation: The main clause has 'would have caught' (Third Conditional), which dictates that the 'if' clause must have Past Perfect tense ('had come').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct sentence structure: If I won the lottery, I ___ buy a new house.
explanation: Second Conditional sentence represents a hypothetical condition. Structure: If + Simple Past ('won'), would + base verb.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Had I known the truth, I ___ differently. (UP B.Ed 2021)
explanation: 'Had I known' is an inverted Third Conditional clause. It requires 'would have + past participle' in the main clause.

subject: English Grammar
text: Complete the sentence: If you don't hurry, we ___ miss the train.
explanation: First Conditional: real future possibility. If + Simple Present ('don't hurry'), Simple Future ('will miss').

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: If the water reaches 100 degrees, it ___.
explanation: Zero Conditional represents scientific fact. Both parts of the sentence take the Simple Present tense.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: If they had invited me, I ___ the party. (UP B.Ed 2023)
explanation: This is a third conditional sentence. If + Past Perfect ('had invited'), would have + Past Participle ('would have attended').

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: If he ___ here, he would solve this problem.
explanation: Second Conditional: hypothetical situation. Subjunctive 'were' is used in the conditional clause for singular subjects too.

subject: English Grammar
text: Complete the sentence: I would help you if I ___ money.
explanation: Second Conditional: structure is 'would + verb' in main clause, Simple Past ('had') in the 'if' clause.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct passive voice: 'The boy killed the snake.' (UP B.Ed 2021)

options.A: The snake is killed by the boy.
options.B: The snake was killed by the boy.
options.C: The snake was kill by the boy.
options.D: The snake had killed by the boy.

explanation: The active sentence is in Simple Past. The passive structure is: object ('The snake') + was/were + past participle ('killed') + by + subject.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct passive voice: 'She is writing a letter.' (UP B.Ed 2022)

options.A: A letter is written by her.
options.B: A letter is being written by her.
options.C: A letter was written by her.
options.D: A letter was being written by her.

explanation: The active sentence is in Present Continuous. Passive structure: object + is/am/are + being + past participle ('is being written').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct active voice of: 'The gate was opened by the watchman.' (UP B.Ed 2019)

options.C: The watchman is opening the gate.
options.D: The watchman has opened the gate.

explanation: Passive voice 'was opened' (Simple Past) changes to active voice in Simple Past 'opened'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct passive voice: 'Who wrote this book?' (UP B.Ed 2020)

options.A: By whom this book was written?
options.B: By whom was this book written?
options.C: Who was written this book by?
options.D: By who was this book written?

explanation: Interrogative sentences starting with 'Who' change to passive with 'By whom' followed by verb-subject inversion ('was this book written?').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct passive voice: 'Close the door.' (UP B.Ed 2018)

options.C: You are asked to close door.

explanation: Imperative sentences representing orders/requests are converted to passive using the formula: Let + subject + be + past participle.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct passive voice: 'They have built a new house.'

options.A: A new house was built by them.
options.B: A new house has been built by them.
options.C: A new house is built by them.
options.D: A new house had been built by them.

explanation: Present Perfect active ('have built') is converted to passive using 'has/have been + past participle' ('has been built').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct passive voice: 'People speak English all over the world.'

options.A: English was spoken all over the world.
options.B: English is spoken all over the world.
options.C: English is being spoken all over the world.
options.D: English has been spoken all over the world.

explanation: Simple Present active ('speak') is converted to passive using 'is/am/are + past participle' ('is spoken'). The vague agent 'by people' is omitted.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct passive voice: 'He will finish the work tomorrow.'

options.A: The work will be finished by him tomorrow.
options.B: The work would be finished by him tomorrow.
options.C: The work will have been finished by him tomorrow.
options.D: The work is finished by him tomorrow.

explanation: Simple Future active ('will finish') changes to passive using 'will be + past participle' ('will be finished').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct active voice of: 'Our team was defeated by the rivals.'

options.C: The rivals were defeating our team.
options.D: The rivals have defeated our team.

explanation: Simple Past passive ('was defeated') converts to active voice in Simple Past ('defeated').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct passive voice: 'Do they teach English here?' (UP B.Ed 2023)

options.A: Is English taught here by them?
options.B: Was English taught here by them?

explanation: Simple Present interrogative ('Do they teach') becomes 'Is + subject + past participle' ('Is English taught').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct passive voice: 'Post this letter.'
explanation: Imperative sentences in the active voice change to passive using the format: Let + subject + be + past participle.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct passive voice: 'Someone has stolen my pen.' (UP B.Ed 2017)
explanation: Present Perfect active ('has stolen') changes to passive using 'has/have been + past participle' ('has been stolen'). Indefinite pronouns like 'someone' are omitted.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct passive voice: 'We are observing the situation.'

options.A: The situation was observed by us.
options.B: The situation is being observed by us.
options.C: The situation has been observed by us.
options.D: The situation is observed by us.

explanation: Present Continuous active ('are observing') changes to passive using 'is/am/are + being + past participle' ('is being observed').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct active voice: 'The window has been broken by John.'
explanation: Present Perfect passive ('has been broken') reverts to Present Perfect active ('has broken').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct passive voice: 'Please help me.' (UP B.Ed 2024)

options.B: You are requested to help me.
options.D: You are ordered to help me.

explanation: Imperative sentences requesting something (usually containing 'Please') are changed to passive using 'You are requested to + base verb'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I am unwell.' (UP B.Ed 2021)

options.A: He said that he was unwell.
options.B: He said that he is unwell.
options.C: He told that he was unwell.
options.D: He said that I was unwell.

explanation: The reporting verb 'said' remains 'said' (not 'told' because there is no direct object). The pronoun 'I' changes to 'he', and 'am' (Present) changes to 'was' (Past).

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: The teacher said to the students, 'The sun rises in the east.' (UP B.Ed 2022)

options.A: The teacher told the students that the sun rose in the east.
options.B: The teacher told the students that the sun rises in the east.
options.C: The teacher said to the students that the sun rises in the east.
options.D: The teacher asked the students that the sun rises in the east.

explanation: When direct speech contains a universal truth or scientific fact, the tense of the verb does not change in indirect speech. 'said to' changes to 'told'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said, 'What a beautiful scene!' (UP B.Ed 2019)

options.A: She exclaimed with joy that it was a very beautiful scene.
options.B: She said that it was a beautiful scene.
options.C: She exclaimed that what a beautiful scene it was.
options.D: She wondered at the beautiful scene.

explanation: Exclamatory sentences are changed to indirect speech using 'exclaimed with joy/grief/wonder'. The sentence becomes assertive, and the exclamation mark is removed.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said to me, 'Where are you going?' (UP B.Ed 2020)

options.A: He asked me where I was going.
options.B: He asked me where was I going.
options.C: He told me where I was going.
options.D: He inquired of me where I am going.

explanation: In indirect speech, interrogatives use 'asked' as the reporting verb, and the sentence word order changes from question (verb-subject) to statement (subject-verb).

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: Ram said, 'I have finished my homework.' (UP B.Ed 2018)

options.A: Ram said that he finished his homework.
options.B: Ram said that he has finished his homework.
options.C: Ram said that he had finished his homework.
options.D: Ram told that he had finished his homework.

explanation: The Present Perfect 'have finished' changes to Past Perfect 'had finished', and first person pronoun 'I' changes to third person 'he' to agree with the speaker.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said to him, 'Please sit down.'

options.A: She told him to please sit down.
options.B: She requested him to sit down.
options.C: She ordered him to sit down.
options.D: She asked him to please sit down.

explanation: Requests in direct speech are changed in indirect speech by using the reporting verb 'requested' and putting the verb in the infinitive form ('to sit down').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: The doctor said, 'Take this medicine twice a day.'

options.A: The doctor advised me to take that medicine twice a day.
options.B: The doctor told me to take this medicine twice a day.
options.C: The doctor ordered me to take that medicine twice a day.
options.D: The doctor said that take this medicine twice a day.

explanation: Imperative sentences containing advice change by using the reporting verb 'advised' followed by an infinitive. 'this' changes to 'that'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I went to London yesterday.'

options.A: He said that he went to London the day before.
options.B: He said that he had gone to London the previous day.
options.C: He said that he has gone to London yesterday.
options.D: He told that he went to London the previous day.

explanation: Simple Past 'went' changes to Past Perfect 'had gone'. The time expression 'yesterday' is converted to 'the previous day' or 'the day before'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: She says, 'I am writing a letter.'

options.A: She says that she was writing a letter.
options.B: She says that she is writing a letter.
options.C: She said that she is writing a letter.
options.D: She says that I am writing a letter.

explanation: If the reporting verb is in the present tense ('says'), the tense of the verb in the reported speech does not change (remains 'is writing'). Only pronouns change.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'Will you help me?' (UP B.Ed 2023)

options.A: He asked if I would help him.
options.B: He asked that if I would help him.
options.C: He inquired if I will help him.
options.D: He told if I would help him.

explanation: For yes/no questions, the conjunction 'if' or 'whether' is used. The modal 'will' changes to 'would', and 'said' becomes 'asked'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'Alas! I am ruined.' (UP B.Ed 2017)

options.A: He exclaimed with sorrow that he was ruined.
options.B: He said sadly that I am ruined.
options.C: He exclaimed with grief that he is ruined.
options.D: He told that he was ruined.

explanation: The word 'Alas!' signifies sorrow, so the reporting verb is changed to 'exclaimed with sorrow'. The simple present 'am' changes to simple past 'was'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: My friend said to me, 'Can you lend me your car?'

options.A: My friend asked me if I could lend him my car.
options.B: My friend asked me that if I could lend him my car.
options.C: My friend told me if I could lend him his car.
options.D: My friend requested me to lend him my car.

explanation: Interrogative sentence starting with modal verb: 'said to' changes to 'asked', linking word is 'if', 'can' changes to 'could', and pronouns shift.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said, 'Honesty is the best policy.'

options.A: She said that honesty was the best policy.
options.B: She said that honesty is the best policy.
options.C: She told that honesty is the best policy.
options.D: She exclaimed that honesty is the best policy.

explanation: 'Honesty is the best policy' is a proverb. Proverbs, general truths, and habitual facts do not undergo a change in tense in indirect speech.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: 'Call the first witness,' said the judge.

options.A: The judge commanded to call the first witness.
options.B: The judge ordered them to call the first witness.
options.C: The judge said that call the first witness.
options.D: The judge urged to call the first witness.

explanation: Commanding or ordering sentences use the reporting verb 'ordered' or 'commanded' followed by an object and an infinitive ('to call the first witness').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I shall go there tomorrow.' (UP B.Ed 2024)

options.A: He said that he should go there tomorrow.
options.B: He said that he would go there the next day.
options.C: He said that he would go there tomorrow.
options.D: He told that he would go there the next day.

explanation: 'I shall' changes to 'he would' in indirect speech because the pronoun shifts to third person singular. 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Neither he nor his friends ___ arrived. (UP B.Ed 2021)
explanation: When subjects are joined by 'neither... nor' or 'either... or', the verb agrees in number with the nearest subject ('his friends' is plural, so we use 'have').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct option: The quality of these mangoes ___ not good. (UP B.Ed 2022)
explanation: The true subject of the sentence is the singular noun 'The quality', not the plural 'mangoes'. Hence, a singular verb ('is') is correct.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Bread and butter ___ my favorite breakfast. (UP B.Ed 2019)
explanation: When two singular nouns are joined by 'and' but express a single, collective idea or food item (bread and butter as a meal), they take a singular verb ('is').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct verb form: Many a student ___ made the same mistake.
explanation: The expression 'Many a' is always followed by a singular noun ('student') and a singular verb ('has').

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Each of the candidates ___ been interviewed. (UP B.Ed 2020)
explanation: 'Each of' is followed by a plural noun but takes a singular verb because the distributives 'each', 'every', 'neither', 'either' are grammatically singular.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Time and tide ___ for no man. (UP B.Ed 2018)
explanation: In this proverbial saying, 'Time and tide' are treated as two separate concepts joined by 'and', requiring the plural verb 'wait'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct verb: Two-thirds of the book ___ been read.
explanation: For fractional expressions, the verb agrees with the noun that follows 'of'. Since 'the book' is singular, the verb is singular ('has').

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: The Prime Minister, along with his cabinet colleagues, ___ arrived. (UP B.Ed 2023)
explanation: Words joined to a singular subject by parenthetical expressions like 'along with', 'as well as', 'together with' do not change the number of the subject. Verb remains singular ('has').

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Mathematics ___ a difficult subject for many.
explanation: Subjects of study ending in '-ics' (Mathematics, Physics, Economics) are singular in form and usage, so they take a singular verb ('is').

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct verb form: A number of students ___ absent today.
explanation: The expression 'A number of' takes a plural verb ('are'), whereas 'The number of' denotes a singular unit and takes a singular verb.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: The committee ___ submitted its report. (UP B.Ed 2017)
explanation: Collective nouns (committee, jury, board) take singular verbs when they act as a single undivided unit, indicated by the singular pronoun 'its'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: The jury ___ divided in their opinions.
explanation: When members of a collective noun act as individuals with differing actions or opinions (indicated by 'their opinions'), it takes a plural verb ('were').

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Physics ___ my favorite subject.
explanation: Names of sciences and subjects ending in '-ics' are singular nouns and must be followed by a singular verb.
